change.title: pr-2-flat
change.description: Optimize spans buffer insertion with eviction during insert
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: optimized_pagination=true returns 500 for any audit log with rows
findings.body: An admin (superuser or global-access member) who sends `?optimized_pagination=true` to an organization that has audit rows gets a 500. `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` reads `datetime` straight off the row (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:838-840) and passes it to `math.ceil`/`math.floor`, which raise TypeError on a datetime. `build_cursor` calls that key on the first result when the cursor value is 0 (src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:121-122) and on the last result (src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:137), so every non-empty page fails. `AuditLogEntry.datetime` is a DateTimeField (src/sentry/models/auditlogentry.py:69). `DateTimePaginator` avoids this by converting the value to a millisecond number (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:233-241), and the new class does not. Use `DateTimePaginator`'s key and cursor conversion, or drop the branch. No test in the PR exercises this branch, which is why it was not caught.

findings.title: member.has_global_access is read on every audit log request, not only the flagged one
findings.body: Line 71 runs before the `use_optimized` check, so it executes on every GET. For a non-superuser, `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated without a None check. `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is documented as None when the user has no membership in the organization (src/sentry/organizations/services/organization/model.py:344-346), and `convert_args` passes that context through without checking it (src/sentry/api/bases/organization.py:286-308). A principal with org:write and no OrganizationMember row (for example an integration token; I did not confirm which token types reach this path) would get an AttributeError and a 500 on the default path, which worked before this PR. Compute `enable_advanced` only inside the `use_optimized` branch, or guard `organization_context.member is not None`.

findings.title: The advanced-path gate uses the stored is_superuser flag, not the active superuser session check
findings.body: This endpoint's own permission grants access to active superusers through `is_active_superuser(request)` (src/sentry/api/bases/organization.py:124), and the same file uses that check elsewhere (src/sentry/api/bases/organization.py:70). The new gate uses `request.user.is_superuser`, the stored flag, which does not require superuser mode to be active. A stored superuser outside superuser mode would then reach the advanced path. Nothing is exposed today because that path currently fails (see the blocker and the negative-offset finding), but fixing the blocker would widen access. Use `is_active_superuser(request)` for this check.

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets reach a negative queryset slice and 500
findings.body: In the `enable_advanced_features` branch, a negative `cursor.offset` becomes `start_offset` and goes straight into `queryset[start_offset:stop]` (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:877-882). Django's QuerySet rejects a negative slice start with an AssertionError, so the request fails with a 500. The offset comes from user input: `Cursor.from_string` accepts negative offsets (src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:52-59). The comments at src/sentry/api/paginator.py:874-880 say that 'the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing' and that 'permissions are checked at the queryset level'. Neither holds: the queryset is scoped only by organization (src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:48), and permission is checked by the endpoint. I did not read Django's source in this review, so the negative-slice premise rests on Django's documented behavior, not a line in this repository. Reject negative offsets with `BadPaginationError`, the pattern `OffsetPaginator` uses (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:286-287), and remove the false comments.

findings.title: BasePaginator now silently turns a negative next-cursor offset into the first page
findings.body: This change affects every BasePaginator subclass in this file (Paginator, DateTimePaginator, OptimizedCursorPaginator). The comment at src/sentry/api/paginator.py:179-181 says negative offsets are allowed. The code clamps offsets for next cursors to 0 (line 182), so the comment is wrong. Before this change, a negative next offset reached `queryset[offset:stop]` and raised. Now the request silently returns the first page with no error. Prev cursors still pass the negative offset through unchanged and still raise. Either reject negative offsets with `BadPaginationError`, or revert this hunk and keep the old behavior.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator.get_result
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:845-911) matches `BasePaginator.get_result` (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:136-215) line for line, apart from the negative-offset branch at lines 877-882. `get_item_key` (lines 838-840) duplicates `Paginator.get_item_key` (lines 222-224). That duplication is how the datetime key bug in the blocker went unnoticed. Put the one branch in a hook or a small override on the base class, and inherit the key function from the paginator the endpoint actually needs.

findings.title: Comment claims negative offsets are supported; nothing in this file does that
findings.body: The comment at src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26-27 says this 'enables efficient reverse pagination from arbitrary positions'. Line 28 does what `int(offset)` already did before this PR. No code in this module treats negative offsets specially. Remove the comment, or make it state that negative offsets are accepted from `from_string` and rejected by the paginators.

findings.title: Spans beyond 1000 are evicted in Redis with no log or metric
findings.body: When a set exceeds 1000 members, `zpopmin` removes the oldest-scored spans at add-buffer.lua:62-64, and nothing else records it. The Python check it replaces logged `Skipping too large segment` and incremented `segment_span_count_exceeded`. That check was removed (in the diff, from the `_load_segment_data` loop; the remaining size check is at src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:441-449). With this PR a segment of 1,200 spans is flushed as its newest 1,000 spans, with no error signal. The metric now never fires, and `max_segment_spans` is stored but never read (src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:150,158). Emit a counter with the number evicted from the Lua path, or keep the Python-side signal. Decide whether silent trimming is intended; the PR body only says 'eviction during insert'.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE sums scores for duplicate members, so eviction order is wrong
findings.body: `zunionstore` without `AGGREGATE` uses SUM (Redis default) for members present in both inputs (add-buffer.lua:47, 53). The scores written by `zadd` are end timestamps (src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:196-199), and `zadd` overwrites them. The union can add a span's score to itself: a span redelivered after its first copy was moved into the target set, while redirects are in effect, lands in both sets during the next union. Its score then doubles, and the eviction at add-buffer.lua:63 no longer orders by end time. Scores are used only for eviction, so the effect is limited to segments over 1000 spans. Add `AGGREGATE MIN` to both unions (add-buffer.lua:47 and 53).

findings.title: Redirect walk cap dropped from 10000 to 1000 and the explanation was removed
findings.body: The loop now stops after 1000 hops (add-buffer.lua:30). The comment that explained what breaks past the limit was removed. A redirect chain longer than 1000 leaves the span in an intermediate set, which then flushes as a separate segment. The `max_redirect_depth` gauge (src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:278-279) will sit at 1000 when this happens, but nothing else signals it. Keep the old cap, or restore the comment and say what happens past it.

findings.title: Glossary still says span-buf:s:* keys are sets
findings.body: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:58 calls `span-buf:s:*` 'the actual set keys'. They are now sorted sets scored by end timestamp (buffer.py:196-199, add-buffer.lua:46-47). The steps at buffer.py:38-40 still say 'set' in the same way. Update the glossary and the steps to say sorted set.

findings.title: Is there a rollout plan for the set-to-sorted-set key type change?
findings.body: The key name `span-buf:s:*` stays the same, but its Redis type changes from set (`sadd`, removed) to sorted set (`zadd`, buffer.py:196-199; add-buffer.lua:46-47). During a rolling deploy, old-version consumers would get WRONGTYPE from `sadd`/`scard`/`sscan` on new keys, and new-version consumers would get WRONGTYPE from `zadd`/`zcard`/`zscan` (buffer.py:434) on old keys. The keys live up to `redis_ttl` (buffer.py:151, default 3600 seconds), so the errors could last that long. Is the rollout drained first, or should the key prefix change?

findings.title: No test covers eviction above 1000 spans or the score ordering it depends on
findings.body: This file only adds `end_timestamp_precise` fields to existing fixtures. Nothing exercises the eviction at add-buffer.lua:58-64, the score ordering after eviction, or the removed flush-time count check. Add a test that inserts more than 1000 spans into one segment and asserts which spans remain after flush.

findings.title: max_segment_spans is now stored but never read
findings.body: After this PR, `max_segment_spans` (src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:150, assigned at line 158) has no reader. Either remove it, or make the eviction size in add-buffer.lua:62-63 take the same value from the caller.

contracts.action: Admin requests with optimized_pagination=true are served by OptimizedCursorPaginator
contracts.equivalent_path: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:85-90 (self.paginate with DateTimePaginator, same order_by and on_results)
contracts.before_after: Same self.paginate call and order_by; only the paginator class and an extra kwarg change. DateTimePaginator turns the datetime into a millisecond number (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:233-241). OptimizedCursorPaginator uses math.floor/ceil on the raw attribute (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:838-840) and does not inherit that conversion.
contracts.visible_effect: Admins get a 500 on any audit log page that has rows, instead of the page.
contracts.failure_mode: TypeError from math.ceil on a datetime, raised while build_cursor computes the first cursor (src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:121-122 and 137).

contracts.action: Every GET on the audit log endpoint evaluates organization_context.member.has_global_access (non-superusers)
contracts.before_after: Before this PR the endpoint never read organization_context.member. After this PR it reads it on every request from a non-superuser, before the optimized_pagination check.
contracts.visible_effect: If member is None, the default audit log page would 500 for that caller.
contracts.open_question: Which principals reach this endpoint with a non-superuser user but no OrganizationMember, and hold org:write? Integration or Sentry App tokens are the likely case.

contracts.action: BasePaginator.get_result computes start_offset for next cursors
contracts.equivalent_path: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:176-179 (the pre-change code, which sliced queryset[offset:stop] with the raw offset)
contracts.before_after: Before: a negative next offset went straight into the slice and raised. After: a next offset below 0 is clamped to 0. Prev offsets are not changed.
contracts.visible_effect: A malformed next cursor with a negative offset returns the first page with no error, for Paginator and DateTimePaginator alike.
contracts.failure_mode: silent wrong page, not an error

contracts.action: add-buffer.lua evicts members beyond 1000 with zpopmin
contracts.equivalent_path: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:441-449 (the remaining flush-time byte-size check, which logs and drops the segment)
contracts.before_after: Before (removed in this PR): a flush-time count check over max_segment_spans logged an error, incremented segment_span_count_exceeded, and dropped the whole segment. After: the oldest-scored spans are removed at insert time; no log, no metric, and the segment is flushed with the rest.
contracts.visible_effect: A segment of more than 1000 spans is flushed as its newest 1000 spans, with no signal.

contracts.action: The Redis type of span-buf:s:* changes from set to sorted set (zadd in process_spans; zunionstore in the Lua script; zscan on flush)
contracts.equivalent_path: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:196-197 before this PR (sadd on the same key name)
contracts.before_after: Before: sadd, sunionstore, scard, sscan on span-buf:s:*. After: zadd, zunionstore, zcard, zscan on the same key names.
contracts.visible_effect: During a mixed-version deploy, consumers on the other version get WRONGTYPE errors on keys written by the first.
contracts.failure_mode: WRONGTYPE from Redis on any command of the other type, for up to redis_ttl seconds
contracts.open_question: Is the rollout drained before the new version starts, or are both versions ever live on the same Redis cluster?

contracts.action: Consumer factory reads end_timestamp_precise from each message
contracts.equivalent_path: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process_segments/message.py:121 (a sibling read of the same key)
contracts.before_after: Before: the field was not read in this consumer. After: a missing key raises KeyError in process_batch and the batch fails.
contracts.visible_effect: A batch containing a message without the field fails.
contracts.open_question: Does the ingest span schema guarantee end_timestamp_precise on every message? I did not read the schema package.

contracts.action: OptimizedCursorPaginator slices the queryset with a negative cursor.offset when enable_advanced_features is set
contracts.equivalent_path: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:884-886 (the else branch, which clamps the next offset to 0)
contracts.before_after: Before this PR there was no negative branch for admins. After: a negative offset goes straight into the queryset slice.
contracts.visible_effect: An admin who sends a negative cursor offset gets a 500.
contracts.failure_mode: AssertionError from Django's negative slice-start check (not read in this repository)
contracts.open_question: Confirm that the pinned Django version rejects a negative slice start, which is the premise of this failure.

summary: Nine files reviewed; no binary or unreadable files. The most serious finding is a blocker: with `optimized_pagination=true`, any admin request against an organization that has audit rows gets a 500, because `OptimizedCursorPaginator` applies `math.ceil` to a datetime. Other findings: the default audit-log path reads `member.has_global_access` without a None check (medium confidence; needs the principal types confirmed); the advanced gate uses the stored `is_superuser` flag instead of `is_active_superuser`; negative cursor offsets reach a queryset slice and 500 (the Django premise was not checked in this repository); the shared `BasePaginator` now silently returns page 0 for a negative next offset; the Redis eviction at 1000 spans is silent, and the metric that used to report it is gone; `ZUNIONSTORE` sums duplicate scores, which corrupts eviction order; the redirect cap dropped from 10000 to 1000; the set-to-sorted-set key change needs a rollout plan; and there are test-coverage and comment/docs gaps. The PR body only describes the span-buffer eviction, so the audit-log, paginator and cursor changes are undocumented. The snapshot has no docs/adr directory, so no ADR check was possible. Nothing was built or run.
